title: Espresso Streusel Coffee Cake Muffins
changes_from_base: A soured-cream batter with butter rubbed into the flour, flavoured with instant espresso and layered with a coffee-cinnamon ribbon and pecan streusel; no fruit.
summary: Soured-cream muffins with espresso in the crumb, a cinnamon-coffee ribbon and a pecan streusel top.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Streusel
steps.text: Pulse both sugars, the 45 g flour, cinnamon, 1 tsp espresso and the cold butter in the food processor until crumbly. Take out 6 tbsp for the middle ribbon, then add the pecans to the processor and pulse until roughly chopped; tip into a bowl.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and line the tin with cases.

steps.title: Wet
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, soured cream, vanilla and 1 tbsp espresso powder until the coffee has dissolved.

steps.title: Rub
steps.text: Pulse the 250 g flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and softened butter in the processor until it looks like damp sand. Tip into a large bowl and fold in the coffee mix until just combined; it will be thick.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Drop 1 tbsp batter into each case and sprinkle with half a tablespoon of the ribbon mix. Share the rest of the batter between the cases and cover with the pecan streusel, pressing it on lightly.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 22-25 min, until golden and a skewer comes out free of raw batter.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Leave 15 min in the tin so the streusel firms up, then lift out.

tips: The most common mistake is not dissolving the espresso; lumps of powder leave bitter spots.
Use instant espresso powder, not ground coffee.
Pecans can be swapped for walnuts, or left out for a nut-free crumb.
storage: Keep in an airtight box at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
